rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=200, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-5 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-4 hr=0.0, warm_start OFF (pure per-image from scratch, n_iter=300) gave rmse=0.00651, ssim=0.938, 197/200 -- no better than warm-started iters. So the amortised warm-start is NOT what pulls scans to over-smooth; from-scratch fits reach the same FBP-consistent plateau. Iters 1-4 (budget, per-scene fit, capacity, warm-start on/off) ALL pinned at hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: structural over-smoothing set by the 128-view FBP self-supervision target, independent of budget/capacity/init. (3) ONE KNOB: lr 1e-3 -> 3e-4 (back to warm_start=True, c=16, n_iter=200 -- identical to iter-2 except lr). (4) HYPOTHESIS: a gentler per-image step size may let the N2I fit settle into a sharper local optimum instead of over-shooting into an over-smoothed mean; if hr rises, the over-smoothing was partly an optimization/step-size artifact. Per the documented ceiling, more likely lr just changes convergence speed and the SAME over-smoothed solution is reached (hr=0), since the target itself is the limiter. (5) BUDGET: identical compute profile to iter-2 (warm-start ep=3 + 200*7.0s + figure ~= 26 min < 30-min wall). (6) Loop continues; iter-6 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: lr up (3e-3), n_iter early-stop (50), pretrain_epochs up (10), unet_c=8, grad_clip variation.
